en: Bats possess excellent eyesight for daytime navigation and use echolocation to hunt insects in the dark.
Rice plants produce their own food from sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide through photosynthesis rather than absorbing mass from soil.
Goldfish possess memories lasting several months, allowing them to learn mazes and recognize specific colors and shapes.
The human brain uses virtually all its regions continuously, with different areas active for various daily tasks.
Butterflies taste their food and suitable egg-laying leaves using specialized sensory organs located on their feet.
Human blood is always red, appearing bright red when oxygenated and dark red when deoxygenated inside veins.
Ostriches dig shallow holes for nests and turn their eggs with their beaks, creating the illusion of buried heads.
Sharks can develop cancer, forming tumors in their cartilage, liver, and other tissues just like other vertebrates.
Human warts are caused by a specific virus, so touching frogs or toads cannot give you warts.
Only young sunflower buds track the sun daily, while mature sunflowers permanently face east to maximize morning warmth.
Harvestmen, commonly called daddy longlegs, are not true spiders and lack venom glands or fangs entirely.
Camels store fat in their humps for energy, relying on their bloodstream and specialized stomachs to retain water.
